      "description": "{\"scope\": \"genuinely-new periodic lattice-sum algorithm and error separation\\n\\nA: `ewald-periodic-potentials-and-particle-mesh-error`.\\n\\nOn a specified 3D torus, finitely many distinct positions x_i and real charges q_i with sum q_i=0 define the mean-zero periodic Poisson distribution -Delta u=4pi(sum q_i delta_xi). Prove the Fourier distribution solution with zero mode fixed and the Gaussian Ewald decomposition of its off-source values/renormalized self energy. Specify the lattice shape, self subtraction, Gaussian parameter alpha, real/reciprocal cutoffs, output convention and arithmetic model. The naive Coulomb lattice sum is conditional; the periodic mean-zero definition controls the summation convention. Prove absolute convergence of the split sums, alpha independence, explicit Gaussian real-tail/reciprocal-tail bounds using lattice shell counts, and differentiated force bounds away from collisions. Include other boundary conventions only by separate explicit formula/proof.\\n\\nFor particle-mesh Ewald specify charge assignment degree/window, periodic grid, discrete Fourier solver, deconvolution restrictions, force differentiation and self correction. Prove error as real cutoff + reciprocal cutoff + assignment/aliasing + mesh differentiation + arithmetic, with actual window Fourier-decay/smoothness assumptions; O(N log N) FFT work alone is not an accuracy theorem. Point-source potentials are singular: any uniform field error is on a collision-free evaluation set, or is stated for a regularized source norm. N-body time integration, thermodynamic limits and singular mean-field limits remain separate.\\n\\nSame-frontier PC-EWALD suppliers: Gaussian Poisson summation (reuse canonical Poisson theorem if its hypotheses fit), torus distribution Green function and zero mode, lattice shell Gaussian estimates, self limit, assignment Fourier aliases and force derivative bounds. Linear owner FFT; PDE owner periodic Poisson if it supplies the exact torus distribution interface; biology owner PIC consumes only the solver guarantee under matching regularization. B: neutral dipole cell, nonneutral zero-mode obstruction, alpha tradeoff at fixed tolerance, source collision, energy/force consistency. Sources: Ewald 1921 https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19213690304 ; Darden–York–Pedersen PME https://doi.org/10.1063/1.464397 ; Essmann et al smooth PME https://doi.org/10.1063/1.470117 . Linear owner FFT; PDE owner periodic Poisson if it supplies the exact torus distribution interface; biology owner PIC consumes only the solver guarantee under matching regularization.       "description": "{\"scope\": [\"Define barycentric rational quotient with support nodes, weights, interpolation-at-support and removable-singularity convention; poles occur at zeros of denominator after cancellation.\", \"Define AAA on a finite distinct sample set: greedy max-residual support, Loewner matrix, minimum-singular-vector weights, tie and zero/rank-deficient branches, budget and residual stopping. Prove support interpolation and finite-sample termination/best small LS residual statements, not uniform off-grid convergence.\", \"Define Floater-Hormann rational interpolation on ordered real nodes with degree parameter and prove no real poles under the exact admissible construction; state an error bound with mesh ratio/smoothness constants.\", \"Define Padé coefficient matching with singular-system/defect branch; prove Taylor order only when moment system solvable, with no analytic-continuation/pole-location guarantee.\"], \"proof_route\": \"Barycentric numerator/denominator algebra; SVD least-squares characterization; alternating denominator sign proof for Floater-Hormann; finite series coefficient matching.\", \"examples\": [\"AAA transfer-function poles\", \"Small sample residual but large off-grid error\", \"Padé denominator failure and Froissart doublet\"]}",
